disagreements.topic: Peer median after dropping BDC/HUBB (lead point 1)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 and agent_5 28.2x (10 peers, no PRY); agent_2 28.1x (11 peers plus Fujikura at its lagged page-basis 28.12x); agent_4 28.1x (11 peers); agent_3 27.5x, because it still keeps BDC (11.3x) and drops VRT. Round 1's 27.5x was the median of 13 names including BDC and HUBB.
disagreements.resolution: The kept set is APH 27.5, TEL 16.8, COHR 29.6, LITE 43.7, CIEN 39.3, FN 25.5, CRDO 28.1, PRY.MI 21.2, VRT 28.3, ANET 43.8, CLS 20.6. Its median is 28.1x (CRDO) on the vendor's adjusted-EPS basis. I keep PRY because it is the only fibre/cable peer and carries the fibre-price risk. Fujikura is not used: there is no consensus EPS to rebase it. BDC and HUBB stay out. agent_3's 27.5x is wrong for this set. Moving to the SBC-consistent basis (next item) gives 28.3x.
disagreements.evidence: Spot checks: StockAnalysis forecast pages re-opened 2026-10-12 show FY EPS APH 2.68/3.33, COHR 9.42/14.05, ANET 4.12/5.22, CRDO 6.31/9.69, VRT 6.74/9.18, all matching the agents. Twelve Data Oct 9 closes are APH 87.24, COHR 312.62, CRDO 216.55, VRT 242.78 and CIEN 449.77, also matching. That covers at least 3 peer multiples per agent, since all five share these names.

disagreements.topic: SBC basis of peer multiples versus Corning core EPS (lead point 2)
disagreements.positions: All five agents verified that Corning core EPS keeps SBC as a cost. All say peer 'adjusted' EPS may exclude SBC, which would make peers look cheaper and bias GLW's value down. Only agent_2 verified one peer (LITE). None adjusted the median. In its round-2 file agent_4 states the direction correctly ('biases my 26x down (conservative), not up'), so the backward statement the lead flagged no longer appears.
disagreements.resolution: Five large peers checked at source. COHR, ANET, CIEN and CRDO add SBC back in adjusted EPS, as LITE does (agent_2). APH keeps SBC in Adjusted Diluted EPS and removes only the excess tax benefit, so it is on Corning's basis. I took annualised latest-quarter SBC after a 21% tax off each confirmed ex-SBC peer's NTM EPS: COHR $0.84/sh, 29.6x to 32.1x; ANET $0.30/sh, 43.8x to 46.6x; CIEN $1.25/sh, 39.3x to 44.1x; CRDO $1.41/sh, 28.1x to 34.3x. LITE moves higher from 43.7x. CRDO, the old median name, moves above the median, so the with-SBC median becomes VRT at 28.3x. VRT, the new median name, keeps SBC in adjusted EPS (citation gate 2026-10-12: its Q2 2026 Ex.99.1 reconciliation adjusts only amortization of intangibles, contingent consideration, restructuring and M&A costs), so it is on Corning's basis at 28.3x. FN, CLS, TEL and PRY were not verified; all sit below the median and stay below it even if they exclude SBC. Decision: put the peer median on a with-SBC basis at 28.3x (estimate), up from 28.1x. It is a small change; the bias was real but mostly affected names already above the median.
disagreements.evidence: COHR FQ4'26 Ex.99.1: share-based compensation add-back $53.9M, 202.2M diluted shares. ANET Q2'26 release: SBC $120.4M added back, 1,276.0M diluted shares. CIEN FQ3'26 Ex.99.1: SBC lines total $57.9M in the adjusted reconciliation, 145.97M diluted shares. CRDO FQ1'27 Ex.99.1: SBC add-back $88.0M, 197.5M non-GAAP diluted shares. APH Q2'26 release: SBC expense $45.4M stays in operating income; only excess tax benefits ($80.5M, $0.06) are excluded. Corning Q2'26 Ex.99 has no SBC line; 10-Q Note 10 SBC is $135M Q2 and $250M H1. VRT Q2'26 Ex.99.1: GAAP-to-adjusted EPS reconciliation lines are amortization of intangibles $0.19, contingent consideration $0.07, restructuring ($0.01) and M&A costs; no SBC line (citation gate, 2026-10-12).

disagreements.topic: Post-horizon risk cuts: size and double counting (lead point 3)
disagreements.positions: Multiples applied: agent_1 26x (27x less 3%), agent_2 26.5x (28.1x less 1.7x), agent_3 26.3x (27.5x less 1.25x), agent_4 26x (27.5x less about 1.2x, plus reverse DCF), agent_5 25.5x (27.5x less 7%). All except agent_2 first took a growth/mix discount to about 27-27.5x and then cut again for long-dated risk. All five keep the AI-capex slowdown out of the multiple as a shared peer risk. agent_5 then deducts that same AI-capex risk (-$16.9) in its DCF leg.
disagreements.resolution: Keeping the AI-capex slowdown out of the multiple is sound. Every peer in the median (ANET, LITE, CIEN, CRDO, CLS, VRT) is at least as exposed as GLW, whose optical business is about 44% of sales. It belongs in the bear tail. Two double counts need correcting. (1) agents 1, 4 and 5 discount for slow segments and growth below the median, then add GLW-specific risks that overlap with it, while their FY28 growth assumption (+23-25% versus +33% in FY27) already decelerates. agent_3 rightly avoided this. (2) agent_5's DCF leg reverses the peer multiple, which already prices the shared AI-capex risk, and then subtracts that risk again. Removing the AI-capex item lifts its DCF from $118.9 to about $135.8 (141.1 - 9.95 + 4.6) and its fair value from $128 to about $131. My reconciled GLW-specific net effect is -$5.9/share, about -4.0% (long_dated_review), so 28.3x becomes about 27.1x.
disagreements.evidence: Sources checked. CRU (Feb 26, 2026): Chinese bare fibre prices rose more than 80% from Nov 2025 to Jan 2026, and preform additions take 'months rather than weeks'; CRU gives no end date for the tightness. CRU OFC 2026 (Apr 14, 2026): Fujikura ¥300bn targeting up to 3x capacity, 'meaningful relief remains quarters away', HCF 'too niche to challenge standard single-mode fibre in the near term', and CPO demand picking up 'considerably' in 2029-2030. Broadband Breakfast (Aug 14, 2026): Prysmian is investing more than $1.2B ($1.02B at Claremont NC, including a new preform plant), will 'more than double its total U.S. output', and plans groundbreaking in mid-September. The online date is NOT stated, so the 2028-29 timing the agents use is judgment. 10-Q Note 2: the $1.0B customer deposit is under a long-term supply agreement 'extending through December 31, 2029', and contract liabilities of $2.7B cover agreements 'typically over periods of up to 10 years'.

disagreements.topic: DCF legs and the 10-year Treasury (lead point 4)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 DCF at 9.6% WACC (rf 5.24%, Damodaran ERP 4.20%) gives $114 before its overlay and $111 after. agent_5 uses cost of equity 10.3% (rf 5.24%, beta 1.12, ERP 4.5% by its own judgment). agents 2 and 4 use the DCF only as a reverse check (fade paths $115-131).
disagreements.resolution: Verified: the treasury.gov daily par yield curve shows 10 Yr 5.24 on 10/09/2026 (3 Mo 4.25). The DCF legs may count. agent_5's 4.5% ERP is a judgment within the conventional range (agent_1's Damodaran 4.20% is lower) and is acceptable as labelled judgment. The intrinsic DCF/fade-path family clusters at about $111-131 at a 9.6-10.3% discount rate, below the relative value. I give it 25% weight (about $111 after my -4.1% overlay on a ~$116 midpoint).
disagreements.evidence: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates CSV, 2026 (10/09/2026 row: 10 Yr 5.24).

disagreements.topic: $296M deposit warrant versus the 15M @ $180 traditional warrant (lead point 5)
disagreements.positions: Round 1 suspected they were the same instrument. In round 2 agent_3 counts them as one; agents 1, 2 and 4 put no warrant dilution in EPS (immaterial); agent_5 counts the warrant once in long_dated_risks (-$0.15).
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed as one instrument. 10-Q Note 2 nets a $296M 'warrant issued to the customer' against the $1.0B deposit, and Note 12 says the 15M @ $180 Traditional Warrant was issued 'in connection with the long-term partnership with a customer'. No agent counts it twice. The $296M is a reduction of contract liability/revenue, not a share count. Treasury-method dilution at $200-210 is about 1.5-2.1M shares (0.2%) and only applies if the stock is above $180. The 3M pre-funded warrant ($500M) is effectively already outstanding. ATM dilution (1.46%) is the only material dilution, and every agent applies it once.

disagreements.positions: agent_1 $106, agent_4 $105 (both reuse round-1's '24x FY27 consensus $4.37' formula), agent_2 $100, agent_5 $100 (lowered from $105 with fair value), agent_3 $98.
disagreements.resolution: $100. The $105-106 levels are anchored on round 1, which set $105 when fair value was $141; at the same ratio to today's $132 it would be about $98. $100 is 19.5x the $5.13 horizon NTM EPS, below the cheapest AI-hardware peers (CLS 20.6x). It is 12.7% below the verified Jul 28, 2026 intraday low of $114.50, which came without fundamental damage, and it is near the late-January 2026 level just after the Meta deal was reported on Jan 27 (Jan 28, 2026 close $104.28; the last pre-deal close was $94.95 on Jan 26).
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data GLW daily OHLC as verified in round 1 (Jul 28 low 114.50; Jan 28 close 104.28); peer multiples above.

disagreements.positions: agent_5: Oct 27, confirmed per StockAnalysis. Others: Oct 27-28 or up to Nov 3, unconfirmed.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed by Corning IR: 'Corning Incorporated Quarter 3, 2026 Earnings Call' on 10/27/2026 at 08:30 ET; the news release posts to Quarterly Results on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. It falls inside the 1-month window.
disagreements.evidence: Corning investor relations events page/feed (event id 1365).

one_month_reasoning: Left at the forecaster mean. Corning IR confirms the Q3 2026 release and call for Oct 27, 2026 at 08:30 ET, inside the window. The guide is core sales $4.9-5.0B and core EPS $0.85-0.89. The last four release-day moves were all negative (-3.3/-5.0/-8.9/-12.1%), too few to tilt the centre. A sigma of about 18-20% for the month fits 68-77% realized vol plus the print.
confidence_reason: Round 2 has converged. Agent fair values are $126-135 (mean $131) and my reconciled $132 sits on that mean. The corrections I verified offset each other: a with-SBC peer median of 28.3x and removing double-counted discounts raise value, while the DCF legs (rf 5.24% verified) pull it down. The only ladder change is a small fattening of the upper tail, where agent_5's tail is thinner than its own volatility implies. Nothing I settled clearly moves the centre, so the mean should stand.
thesis_break_reason: $100 is 19.5x the $5.13 Oct-2027 NTM EPS and 22.9x verified FY27 consensus of $4.37. That is below the cheapest AI-hardware peer (CLS 20.6x) and 12.7% below the verified Jul 28, 2026 intraday low of $114.50, a drop that came without fundamental damage. A close there would most likely mean 2027-28 EPS is being cut (hyperscaler or carrier deferrals, a fibre price roll-over as Prysmian/Fujikura capacity lands, or a slip in the $20B/$30B Springboard path), not 70%-vol noise. The $105-106 levels are anchored on round 1's formula from a $141 fair value.
key_drivers: Valuation: GLW trades at 38.2x consensus NTM EPS ($4.10). Peers trade at a median of 28.3x on an SBC-consistent basis (COHR/ANET/CIEN/CRDO/LITE verified ex-SBC and adjusted; APH verified with-SBC). Less about 4% for GLW-specific post-horizon risks, that is about 27.1x on $5.13 Oct-2027 NTM EPS = $139 relative value. The DCF legs at a 9.6-10.3% discount rate (verified 10Y 5.24%) give about $111.

Execution against verified guidance: Q3 guide core EPS $0.85-0.89 (+28%) on sales $4.9-5.0B (+16%), reported Oct 27, 2026 (confirmed by Corning IR). The first Q4 guide tests the $20B end-2026 run rate.

Fibre cycle after the horizon: CRU shows prices up >80% in China on a preform squeeze with relief 'quarters away'. Prysmian (>$1.2B, more than doubling U.S. output, new preform plant) and Fujikura (¥300bn, up to 3x) are adding capacity whose online dates are not disclosed. A 50% chance of a partial price reset costs about $5/share in the horizon multiple.

Contract visibility and funding: a $1.0B deposit LTA runs through Dec 31, 2029; contract liabilities are $2.7B; a $2B ATM (1.46% dilution) is the only material dilution, and the $296M deposit warrant is the same 15M @ $180 warrant (counted once).
Extreme volatility (realized 68-77%) keeps the 12-month distribution very wide whatever the centre.

fair_value.reason: No-DCF rule (Kilian 2026-10-21 13:50Z: no DCF leg for any researched name except the neoclouds), applied 2026-10-22: drops the 25% intrinsic DCF/fade-path leg ($111.2): relative leg $139.3 alone = $139.3 (was $132.0; other legs renormalised, nothing else changed). Original: Estimate. (1) Relative, 75% weight: with-SBC peer median 28.3x x $5.13 Oct-2027 NTM core EPS (0.25 x FY27 $4.37 + 0.75 x FY28E $5.38; FY28E = 4.37 x 1.25 x 0.985 for the ATM) = $145.2. No separate growth/mix discount, because the decelerating FY28 growth and the explicit Glass Innovations risk already cover it. (2) Intrinsic, 25% weight: the DCF/fade-path family (agent_1 $114 at 9.6% WACC with the verified 5.24% 10Y; agent_2 $115 at 10%; agent_4 $116-131) has a midpoint of about $116, x (1 - 0.041 overlay) = $111. 0.75 x 139.3 + 0.25 x 111.2 = $132.3, about $132. One consistent SBC basis: SBC is a cost in Corning core EPS (no add-back) and in peers adjusted to with-SBC; no extra SBC dilution. ATM dilution is counted once; the deposit warrant and the NVIDIA warrant are one immaterial instrument.

On an SBC-consistent basis peers trade at a median of 28.3x NTM. GLW deserves about 27x after GLW-specific post-horizon risks, mainly a fibre price reset as Prysmian and Fujikura capacity lands. The DCF legs, now verified against a 5.24% 10-year yield, pull value toward $111. The AI-capex digestion risk is correctly left in peer multiples and the bear tail. Q3 results come Oct 27 (confirmed), and the thesis breaks at $100.
